hints: This city sits on the River Seine in northern France.
The Louvre museum and its glass pyramid are here.
puzzles.reveal: Pont Neuf means ‘New Bridge’ in French, but it is actually the oldest surviving bridge in Paris.

hints: This city lies on the eastern side of Honshu, Japan’s largest island.
Its Shibuya district is famous for a scramble crossing where pedestrians cross in every direction.
puzzles.reveal: Tokyo used to be called Edo. It was renamed in 1868; its new name means ‘Eastern Capital’.

hints: This city is on the Atlantic coast of the United States.
The Statue of Liberty stands on an island in its harbor.
puzzles.reveal: Manhattan’s famous street grid was planned in 1811, but it took about 60 years to build it as far north as 155th Street.

hints: This city lies on Spain’s Mediterranean coast.
Antoni Gaudí’s Sagrada Família basilica is here.
puzzles.reveal: Barcelona’s Eixample blocks have their corners cut off at 45-degree angles. Planner Ildefons Cerdà designed them that way to make it easier for people and traffic to move around.

hints: This city is on Australia’s east coast, built around a large natural harbor.
Bondi Beach is one of this city’s famous beaches.
puzzles.reveal: The Sydney Opera House’s roof shells are all shaped from sections of a single sphere. That shared geometry helped turn its unusual design into something engineers could build.

hints: This city is in New England, in the northeastern United States.
Its Freedom Trail links historic sites associated with the American Revolution.
puzzles.reveal: Boston’s Back Bay really was a bay. Much of the neighborhood stands on former tidal water that was filled in during the 1800s.

hints: This city is on Canada’s Pacific coast, close to the United States border.
Its Gastown neighborhood is known for a steam clock.
puzzles.reveal: Stanley Park opened in 1888, when Vancouver’s population was just 6,065 people.

hints: This city stands beside the Río de la Plata estuary in South America.
The pink Casa Rosada, home to Argentina’s presidential office, is here.
puzzles.reveal: Buenos Aires has a bookstore inside a former theater. El Ateneo Grand Splendid became a bookshop in 2000, keeping the ornate dome and turning the stage into a place to have coffee.

hints: This city is in the western, peninsular part of Malaysia.
Its PETRONAS Towers are connected by a skybridge.
puzzles.reveal: Two rivers meet in the heart of Kuala Lumpur. Masjid Jamek, one of the city’s oldest mosques, stands at the meeting point of the Klang and Gombak rivers.

hints: This city is on the Atlantic coast of the United States.
The Statue of Liberty stands on an island in its harbor.
puzzles.reveal: Manhattan’s famous street grid was planned in 1811, but it took about 60 years to build it as far north as 155th Street.

puzzles.reveal: Manhattan’s famous street grid was planned in 1811, but it took about 60 years to build it as far north as 155th Street.

hints: This city in Western Europe uses canals to shape much of its historic center
Anne Frank’s hiding place is now a museum in this city.
puzzles.reveal: Amsterdam's canal arcs were planned. In the 1600s, the city expanded by draining marshland and building concentric canals, creating space for new streets and houses.

hints: This city lies inland, in the central-western part of Brazil.
Built to become the national capital, it replaced Rio de Janeiro in 1960.
puzzles.reveal: From above, Brasília’s planned layout resembles a bird in flight. Urban planner Lúcio Costa designed the city’s overall shape, while architect Oscar Niemeyer designed its landmark government buildings.
